comparisons.peer_topic: Operating cash flow and drivers in 2024
comparisons.peer_summary: Net cash provided by operating activities was $3 billion in 2024, primarily driven by net income of $1.6 billion, non-cash adjustments of $3.5 billion, and net cash outflows of $2.1 billion from changes in operating assets and liabilities, including a $1.9 billion increase in accounts receivable due to higher year-end revenue and a $1.5 billion increase in inventories to support new product ramps.
comparisons.comparison: Both QCOM and AMD disclose significant increases in accounts receivable as a primary driver of operating cash flow outflows in fiscal 2024, attributing the increases to higher year-end revenues. QCOM reports a partial offset to its positive operating cash flow from an increase in accounts receivable due to higher revenues, while AMD reports a $1.9 billion increase in accounts receivable driven by higher revenue in the last month of 2024 compared to 2023 as a major component of net cash outflows from changes in operating assets and liabilities.

sentences.text: Net changes in our operating assets and liabilities positively impacted our operating cash flows in fiscal 2024 primarily from an increase in accrued customer incentives, which included the impact of timing of related payments, and an increase in accounts payable due to timing and amount of inventory purchases, partially offset by an increase in accounts receivable due to higher revenues.

The primary drivers of the changes in operating assets and liabilities included a $1.9 billion increase in accounts receivable driven primarily by higher revenue in the last month of 2024 compared to the last month of 2023, and a $1.5 billion increase in inventories driven primarily by a build of inventory to support the ramp of new products in advanced process nodes.

peer_results.rationale: The retrieved AVGO candidates do not provide a comparable narrative of net operating cash flow changes driven by operating assets and liabilities in the same manner. avgo_2024_7_D071 focuses on specific balance sheet caption changes (decrease in AR, increase in other current assets/liabilities) rather than a holistic view of operating cash flow drivers, and avgo_2024_7_D076 relates to financing activities.

The retrieved INTC candidates do not provide a directly comparable analysis of net changes in operating assets and liabilities impacting operating cash flows. intc_2024_7_D107 discusses liquidity management actions (timing adjustments, factoring) as a risk/driver rather than reporting the net impact of these changes on the cash flow statement, and intc_2024_7_D109 focuses on the comparison between net income/non-cash items and the year-over-year decrease in operating cash flows, lacking the specific working capital component breakdown found in the target.

comparisons.peer_summary: In 2024, cash provided by operating activities increased compared to 2023, primarily driven by net income adjusted for non-cash items, increases in accounts payable, accrued expenses, and other current liabilities (largely due to customer prepayments), partially offset by an increase in receivables.
comparisons.comparison: Both QCOM and MU identify increases in receivables as a factor offsetting other positive drivers in operating cash flows during fiscal 2024. QCOM notes an increase in accounts receivable due to higher revenues, while MU reports an increase in receivables that partially offset the positive impact of increases in accounts payable and accrued expenses.

sentences.text: Net changes in our operating assets and liabilities positively impacted our operating cash flows in fiscal 2024 primarily from an increase in accrued customer incentives, which included the impact of timing of related payments, and an increase in accounts payable due to timing and amount of inventory purchases, partially offset by an increase in accounts receivable due to higher revenues.

The increase in cash provided by operating activities for 2024 as compared to 2023 was primarily due to net income in 2024 adjusted for non-cash items, the effect of an increase in accounts payable and accrued expenses and an increase in other current liabilities largely due to customer prepayments to secure product supply, partially offset by an increase in receivables.

comparisons.peer_summary: Cash provided by operating activities increased in fiscal year 2024 compared to 2023 due to revenue growth, while the accounts receivable balance in 2024 included $557 million from customer payments received ahead of invoice due dates.
